title: Debt sustainability analysis for euro area sovereigns: a methodological framework
summary: This ECB Occasional Paper introduces a comprehensive debt sustainability analysis (DSA) framework for euro area sovereigns, consisting of three building blocks: deterministic DSA (benchmark and shock scenarios), stochastic DSA (probabilistic approach), and other indicators capturing liquidity and solvency risks. The framework is designed as a warning system for fiscal surveillance under the Stability and Growth Pact.
key_points: The DSA framework contains three main building blocks: deterministic DSA, stochastic DSA, and additional short/long-term indicators
Deterministic DSA evaluates debt projections under benchmark and adverse narrative shock scenarios over a 10-year horizon
Stochastic DSA provides probability assessments for debt levels exceeding thresholds, debt stabilization failure, and overall uncertainty
Short-run liquidity risks are assessed via net financing needs and a composite refinancing ease index
Medium/longer-run risks include: public debt maturity structure, contingent liabilities scope, net financial position, and governance/political risk
The three blocks are summarized in a heat map to provide overall debt sustainability risk guidance
Framework incorporates EU fiscal governance requirements under the Stability and Growth Pact
why_it_matters: This methodological paper establishes the analytical framework used by the ECB to assess sovereign debt sustainability risks across euro area countries. It does not contain current market-relevant data but provides the analytical approach that informs ECB fiscal surveillance under the Stability and Growth Pact and could generate policy warnings for member states.
macro_context: The paper addresses sovereign debt sustainability methodology for euro area countries, relevant to understanding fiscal risks that could affect sovereign bond markets. It is methodological in nature, published April 2017, and does not contain current macro data or market catalysts.
